questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Already having a basis of the local language and therefore being able to gain academically. Interest in the specific school (historical site, their tradition og landscape architecture).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: tough (personally and academically) but worth it. a great experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It took quite some time, energy and ressources to get an overview of the information needed. Practical and academically. When the exchange is taking place in one's third language in stead of English which is my second language, it is of course more difficult. Also takes up more time and energy which is added to thee existing work load of the semester. Therefore it has at times felt chaotic. Many actors and people to link between. Specifically it was difficult to understand which courses that corresponded to which courses of the learning agreement since it didn't always have the same name or description. Some kind of meeting where the semester would ne presented and explained in relation to learning agreement would have been extremely helpful. Also having cleared out expectation for Erasmus students when arriving compared to normal students would have taken some stress away.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was shown around at the property and was helped getting acces to online platform of the school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: the responsible International office not always available. other students wanting to be helpfull but low age and lack of travel experience meant that they were not always welcoming and including. only a few. after some time it got better.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If one was ok with shared housing where you don't know the flatmates in advance it would be easy with help from the school. This was not my case to I went searching on my own which was more complicated.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: they were very helpful but I didn't choose this option.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: all courses was mandatory so easy in that sense.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: by mail and simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: mail correspondence with the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: overall very expanding in every sense.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: challenging, academically intersting and very different from my host institution. very positive.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: more personal, less structured, more chaotic. no sense of control over ones schedule. very time demanding. therefore I was pushed far and gained a lot. however more transparency in the schedule, deadlines and expectations would have meant a better and more respectful experience overall.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: gardening internship, urban analysis, ecology / managing the living, garden of the future, art workshop, analysis /reading of the landscape, botanics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Garden of the future "le Jardin du futur". A course that is artistic, full of abstractions and expression forms and reflexions that would never take place at UCPH.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: plenty of communities to join if one is interested.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: gardening, music, drawing, parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: what is of interest of the above.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: took some time but its the fun part to see the differences.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: you have to be quite forward minded and extroverted in order to make friends. don't be afraid of inviting yourself in.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: them being ok with having so little control over their study life and their time in general. less self managing since the teachers are deciding every minute of the day (the day is until 18-19 in the evening often).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: craziness, creativeness, fun chaotic, not afraid of sneaking up, making noise, being playful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: don't be afraid to take space socially even with language barriers. take notes all the time to gain some structure and information. ask what are the expectations for you to every teacher to minimize stress.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: be part of facebook + WhatsApp group chat.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the last months where I finally felt part of the class and spoke the language quite well and felt inspired by the course Le jardin du futur.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: lack of trust in myself (you have to be in a good place when taking off since this is really a challenge to take on).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: do it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
